description:
The Master of Accountancy and Data Analytics program is a non-thesis professional program that gives accounting students the data analytics skills they need to be successful in the accounting profession.

This program is designed to develop the data analytics skills necessary to ask the right questions and to find appropriate answers from the data. Students learn how to analyze and understand large amounts of data from different sources; how to identify and find patterns, trends and other information in the data; and how to communicate their findings.

Students in this STEM-designated program receive training in the technologies that are quickly becoming standard in the business world, including:

Alteryx
artificial intelligence
blockchain
robotic process automation
Tableau
Python
SQL
The program is typically completed in nine months (fall and spring semesters).

This program satisfies the 150-hour requirement for CPA licensure in Arizona and other states.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate and graduate programs and the School of Accountancy are all accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The MFA in acting is an intensive three-year program focused on the development of the actor as an artist, artisan and entrepreneur. The goal is to develop artists with the desire and ability to create their own work and who are self-generating, self-sustaining and self-producing.
The curriculum is studio-based and experiential. The faculty is a team of artists and educators who are nationally and internationally recognized. The training combines classical and contemporary methods, with a strong emphasis on new work, devised work, and interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary creation.
The master's degree program culminates in a public performance of an original work created by the student, the applied project.
The program is distinguished by its small class size (typically three to five students are admitted each year); its one-on-one mentorship by faculty; and its focus on new work development, community engagement and social activism through performance.
Accreditation status: National Association of Schools of Theatre, Accredited

description: The Master of Science in addiction psychology provides students with an in-depth understanding of the psychology and neurobiology of addiction and its treatment. The program's curriculum centers on evidence-based practice to prepare students for careers as clinicians, researchers and leaders in the field of addiction. The program also provides the foundational coursework required for licensure as a substance abuse counselor in the state of Arizona. The curriculum places an emphasis on a multicultural and systemic framework for understanding addiction. Students are challenged to develop into self-reflective, ethical and culturally competent professionals who work with and advocate for diverse individuals and families. The program offers two tracks: 1. A nonthesis track with an emphasis on clinical work. Students in this track complete a clinical practicum and internship in a community-based setting. 2. A thesis track that offers students opportunities to become involved in research while they are in the program, and these students complete an empirical thesis under the mentorship of a faculty member. All students are required to complete a 100-hour practicum and a 600-hour internship for a total of 700 hours of clinical experience.

The advanced analytics in higher education graduate certificate program provides students with the foundational skills to conduct advanced analytics within a higher education context. In this program, students develop the analytic and data science skills necessary to make informed, evidence-based decisions.

The coursework focuses on data management and warehousing, predictive analytics, and data visualization. The program addresses the need for institutional researchers, student affairs professionals, and higher education administrators to be data literate and capable of using advanced analytic methods to improve institutional effectiveness and student success. The certificate program can also serve as a gateway to the Doctor of Education in leadership and innovation program.
Program name: Advanced Analytics in Higher Education, Graduate Certificate

description:
The Master of Science in aerospace engineering is a research-oriented program in which students work closely with a faculty advisor to design a research project, conduct research and write and defend a thesis.

Students can customize their educational experience by choosing courses in one of six specialization areas: acoustics and structural dynamics, advanced manufacturing and materials, autonomous and intelligent systems, computational fluid dynamics and aerodynamics, space systems, and thermofluid systems.

Students can enhance their knowledge by becoming involved with cutting-edge research opportunities, nationally recognized faculty, and state-of-the-art research facilities. They develop a deeper understanding of aerospace engineering through an advanced course of study and research in preparation for doctoral studies or a career in research and development in industry or government.

The aerospace engineering doctoral program in the School for Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy provides students with an education with a broad background in aerospace engineering and a deep research experience in their chosen specialization. Students can choose a focus area including: aerodynamics and fluid dynamics; aerospace structures and materials; astrodynamics and space systems; dynamics and control; and propulsion and combustion. The program provides the necessary skills and knowledge for students to make original contributions to the field of aerospace engineering. The program faculty members have extensive experience and are internationally recognized in their fields of research. They are also excellent instructors and mentors. This is a research-intensive degree program. Students are expected to carry out research under the guidance of a faculty advisor and to disseminate their research findings through conference presentations and archival journal publications. The PhD in aerospace engineering is granted upon a successful defense of the dissertation, which is a significant, original contribution to the state of the art in the aerospace engineering field.

The Master of Arts in American Indian studies with a concentration in cultural resource revitalization and sustainability is a unique program designed to provide a broad understanding of the historical and contemporary legal, political, social and cultural contexts shaping American Indian life and to give students the knowledge needed to pursue advanced study or a career in Native leadership. The program focuses on:
cultural resource management
language revitalization
legal and policy issues related to Native American self-determination and Indigenous rights
Students develop practical, real-world skills through the program's strong internship component. American Indian Studies at ASU actively supports students through every step of their graduate school journey, from advising and mentorship to graduation and beyond. This approach has led to exceptional completion rates: 90% of students in the master's degree program graduate within two years.

The degree program is distinctive because of the breadth of faculty research interests, an interdisciplinary approach and an emphasis on connecting research to the needs of Native communities. The faculty's work in community-based research offers students valuable experience working with tribal communities. The curriculum allows students to take courses from other programs at ASU, providing a solid foundation and in-depth training on the historical context, legal complexity and diverse cultural knowledge needed to address the challenges and possibilities facing Native American and other Indigenous communities.
Program name: American Indian Studies (Cultural Resource Revitalization and Sust), Master of Arts

description:
The American Indian studies MA program offers a concentration in Indigenous rights and social justice that focuses on the individual and collective rights of American Indians and other Indigenous peoples. The concentration critically analyzes complex issues of tribal sovereignty, self-determination, human rights, and decolonization through the lens of Indigenous critical theory and Indigenous-centered research methodologies.

The curriculum is interdisciplinary in nature. Students examine the legal, political, social, cultural, environmental and economic factors that shape Indigenous rights and their pursuit of social justice from both historical and contemporary perspectives.

A key feature of the Indigenous rights and social justice concentration is its hands-on approach. Through research, coursework and the required internship, students have the opportunity to engage in rights- and justice-based projects with Indigenous nations, communities and organizations, gaining real-world experience and marketable skills. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in tribal governments, Indigenous-led community organizations, federal and state agencies, and nonprofit organizations working in human rights, environmental justice, cultural resources protection, education and community development.
Program name: American Indian Studies (Indigenous Rights and Social Justice), Master of Arts

description:
The Master of Arts in American Indian studies with a concentration in tribal leadership and governance is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with the intellectual and practical skills to conduct research and leadership work in American Indian studies and with Indigenous communities. The program is designed for students who want to work with Indigenous nations in leadership positions or in program development and management as well as for those who wish to pursue a doctoral degree.

Graduates are equipped with the knowledge needed to assume leadership and administrative roles in a number of areas, including:

tribal, federal and state governments
business
cultural resource management
education
health care
social services

The program also has a strong research focus that prepares students to carry on to a doctoral program, particularly the ASU doctoral program in justice and social inquiry.
Program name: American Indian Studies (Tribal Leadership and Governance), Master of Arts

description:
The Master of Arts degree program in American Indian studies with a concentration in visual and oral culture is a transdisciplinary program focused on the study of the oral and visual traditions of American Indian peoples. This includes the study of language, literature, philosophy and religious thought as expressed orally, as well as the study of art, media and material culture. The concentration is designed to prepare students for doctoral study in fields that engage American Indian studies, such as history, law and literature, and for a number of professions, including those in which a deep understanding of American Indian peoples and their expressive cultures is vital.

Coursework includes a core curriculum that provides a solid foundation for understanding the major theoretical and methodological approaches to American Indian studies, along with a number of electives from which students can choose to tailor their program to fit their own interests. Students work with faculty members from a range of academic disciplines, and they have the opportunity to participate in independent research, to work on projects in the American Indian community and to develop a deep and holistic understanding of American Indian cultures and the challenges facing American Indian communities today.
Program name: American Indian Studies (Visual and Oral Culture), Master of Arts

description:
The MA program in anthropology provides students with a graduate-level background in the various subdisciplines of anthropology. Students receive a breadth of training but specialize in a subdiscipline for their thesis or research paper. The program emphasizes professional development and encourages students to present at professional conferences and to publish their work.

Students may choose to pursue research in any of the subdisciplines represented in the school: archaeology, bioarchaeology, evolutionary anthropology, linguistic anthropology, medical anthropology, sociocultural anthropology, and urban and environmental anthropology.

The program is ideal for students wishing to pursue a doctoral degree or to work as professional anthropologists in government or the private sector.

The master's degree program culminates with a thesis or research paper.

Note: this program is for students intending to earn the doctoral degree. A separate application is required for admission to the doctoral program. For students not admitted to the doctoral program, the terminal MA in anthropology is not offered.

The PhD program in anthropology prepares students for careers in research and teaching and for the application of anthropological knowledge to contemporary global problems. The program has a strong commitment to the four-field approach, integrating archaeology, evolutionary anthropology, sociocultural anthropology and linguistics, with in-depth training within one of six areas of study:
archeology
bioarchaeology
evolutionary anthropology
global health
medical anthropology
sociocultural anthropology
The anthropology doctoral program, housed in the School of Human Evolution and Social Change, is consistently ranked among the top programs in the nation by the National Research Council. In addition to a variety of research and teaching interests, the faculty have a wide range of regional specializations, including the American Southwest, Mesoamerica, South America, Europe, Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, South Asia and Oceania. Many faculty have established collaborative research programs that provide graduate students with an array of opportunities for field, laboratory and collections research.
Graduates are highly competitive for tenure-track academic appointments in top-tier universities as well as for research positions in government and the private sector.

The Master of Science in applied behavior analysis at Arizona State University's Tempe campus provides a high-quality graduate learning experience for those who want to work with individuals with behavioral needs. The MS program prepares students to become scientist-practitioners of applied behavior analysis. Graduates from our program have the coursework and practicum experience to apply for certification as a Board Certified Behavior Analyst®. The ABAI has verified the following courses toward the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® or Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst® examination. Applicants will need to meet additional requirements before they can be deemed eligible to take the examination. In this MS program, students develop an understanding of the principles of behavior and the procedures derived from those principles. Students also acquire skills in the application of these principles and procedures to improve the quality of life for individuals, families and communities. The MS program follows a mentorship model, in which each student is assigned a faculty mentor for the duration of the program. Students can expect to receive regular, direct guidance from their mentors in a combination of research and practicum activities. The curriculum consists of a combination of core applied behavior analysis content, practicum, and research experiences culminating in a required thesis.
Accreditation status: The Association for Behavior Analysis International has verified the following courses toward the coursework requirements for eligibility to take the Board Certified Behavior Analyst® or Board Certified Assistant Behavior Analyst® examination. Applicants will need to meet additional requirements before they can be deemed eligible to take the examination.
Program name: Applied Behavior Analysis, Master of Science

description:
The Master of Arts in applied leadership and management is a transdisciplinary program focused on the knowledge and skills needed for effective leadership in the 21st century. The curriculum provides a foundation in leadership theory and practice, and it integrates current knowledge from several disciplines: communication, leadership and interdisciplinary studies, project management, and organizational leadership.

The program includes core coursework, electives and an applied project that allow students to synthesize and apply their learning. The core coursework emphasizes developing skills related to research, ethics, decision-making, conflict resolution, global leadership, and organizational behavior and communication. Electives provide opportunities for students to build on specific areas of interest. The applied project requires students to develop a project directly applicable to their career and to demonstrate mastery of the leadership concepts and strategies covered in the coursework.

Concentration name: History, theory and criticism of architecture; Energy performance and building systems
description:
The architectural studies doctoral program offers advanced scholarly study, culminating in a dissertation, on the subject of the built environment. This program provides students a setting for the critical study of architecture from the perspectives of the humanities, the sciences and the professions.

The doctoral program in architectural studies focuses on the advanced study of the built environment and offers two distinct specializations: history, theory and criticism of architecture, and energy performance and building systems.

Students in the history, theory and criticism specialization pursue interdisciplinary research focusing on architectural history and theory, landscape and urbanism, and technology and culture in various global contexts. The specialization is linked to the activities and faculty of the Master of Science in architecture program.

Students in the energy performance and building systems specialization conduct research on the analysis, simulation and design of high-performance buildings. Students' research is closely aligned with the research interests of faculty in building science, including energy efficiency, daylighting, building envelope, materials, HVAC systems and sustainability.

The PhD in architectural studies program is a small, selective program designed to produce graduates who become university professors and researchers as well as research leaders in industry and government.

The Master of Architecture is a professional degree program that prepares students for careers in architecture and for professional licensure. Graduates possess the skills and knowledge to work in a variety of roles in the design and construction industries and in a wide range of allied design fields. The MArch is accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board, which is the sole agency authorized to accredit professional degree programs in architecture in the United States. The program offers a dynamic curriculum that integrates design, research and practice. It is structured to provide students with a strong foundation in the art and science of architecture, as well as the opportunity to specialize in areas of interest through a rich array of advanced studios and seminars. The program also has strong connections with the local professional community, offering students a variety of opportunities to interact and work with practicing architects. Students in the MArch program may also have the opportunity to participate in design studios, summer programs, internships and research opportunities around the globe through a large and diverse set of international programs and professional connections.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board

description:
The Master of Fine Arts in art is a three-year program that offers students the opportunity for advanced creative study in a variety of disciplines within the visual arts.

The School of Art in the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts offers a stimulating environment for graduate study, with dedicated faculty, excellent facilities and a dynamic community of fellow artists. The program's proximity to the robust art scenes of Phoenix and Los Angeles provides a unique context for engagement with the contemporary art world.

The program emphasizes the development of a mature and high-quality body of creative work and a supportive intellectual context for that work. Students benefit from the significant resources of a Research I university, including its libraries, museum and collections. Graduates are prepared for careers as professional artists and for teaching positions at the university level. Ultimately, the MFA program aims to produce self-aware and critically engaged graduates who demonstrate excellence and innovation in their respective fields.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description: The MA in art education in the School of Art is a 30-credit hour program that includes opportunities for students to learn from and work with nationally and internationally recognized faculty in art education and in a variety of other art disciplines. This program prepares students for leadership positions in schools, museums and communities. The program provides the opportunity to develop skills and knowledge in art education research and pedagogy and contemporary and historical art education practices. The program also provides coursework to develop students' knowledge in the areas of art history, art criticism, aesthetics and studio art, including new media, digital technologies, creative and cultural industries and arts-based research methods.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description:
The Master of Science in artificial intelligence in business provides students with a solid foundation in the artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques needed to create business value.

The curriculum focuses on the application of AI and ML to business problems and the practical implications for business strategy, performance and models. The program is specifically designed to serve students and working professionals from both technical and business backgrounds who are interested in the applications of AI in business.

For students with a technical background, the program allows them to apply their knowledge to specific business problems and learn to use AI and ML to drive business value. For students with a business background, the program enables them to understand and leverage the power of AI to transform organizations.

This transdisciplinary program is a collaboration between the W. P. Carey School of Business and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering, leveraging the world-class expertise of both schools to offer a unique, state-of-the-art curriculum.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top-ranked business schools in the country, with undergraduate and graduate business programs, including the MBA, consistently ranking among the best in the nation.
Program name: Artificial Intelligence in Business, Master of Science

description:
The MA program in Asian languages and civilizations with a concentration in Japanese is designed to provide students with advanced training in the study of Japanese language, linguistics, culture,literature and civilization and to prepare students for either doctoral work at other institutions or employment in a variety of fields, including business, education and government.

The program features an interdisciplinary approach to East Asia and provides the opportunity for students to work with a range of faculty members specializing in Asian studies across the university.

The curriculum covers a broad range of topics, including the study of modern and classical Japanese, Japanese literary and cultural studies, and Japanese linguistics. Students pursuing this degree must choose one of three focuses: language and linguistics, literature and culture, or pedagogy.
Program name: Asian Languages and Civilizations - Japanese, Master of Arts

description:
The Doctor of Audiology (AuD) program at Arizona State University is a four-year, post-baccalaureate degree program focused on the science of hearing, balance and related disorders, and is designed to produce highly skilled audiologists. The program also focuses on the evaluation and treatment of hearing and balance disorders in adults and children.

Students receive a strong foundation in the basic sciences of hearing and balance and extensive training in the diagnosis and management of hearing and balance disorders. The AuD degree is a clinical doctorate designed to prepare students for professional careers in audiology. ASU's AuD program has been ranked among the best in the nation by U.S. News & World Report for more than a decade.

Our clinical training provides an exceptional breadth and depth of experiences, a result of our world-class faculty, our multiple on-campus clinics and our outstanding relationships with clinical facilities throughout the Phoenix metropolitan area. Students gain experience in a variety of settings, including hospitals, private practices and schools.

The AuD curriculum provides students with the academic and clinical background to meet the requirements for the Certificate of Clinical Competence in Audiology from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association and state licensure in audiology. Students complete a program of study that includes a minimum of 96 credit hours of academic coursework and clinical practicum. The curriculum includes a strong scientific foundation and a comprehensive clinical education.

Upon completion of this program, students are highly trained in their clinical abilities and prepared to pursue professional careers.
Accreditation status: The Doctor of Audiology (AuD) education program in audiology {residential} at Arizona State University is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language-Pathology of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard, #310, Rockville, MD 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.

description:
The Doctor of Behavioral Health with a clinical concentration is a professional doctoral degree focused on preparing master's-level clinicians to be leaders in integrated behavioral health care. The degree provides advanced training for a new kind of health care professional: the behavioral clinician who will work as part of a team alongside physicians and nurses to provide whole-person health care.

The focus is on medical settings, such as primary care, specialty medical clinics and hospitals, where most patients with mental and behavioral health problems present. In the DBH program, students learn a patient-centered, evidence-based, cost-effective curriculum that provides the clinical and business skills to improve medical outcomes, reduce health care costs and create new models of integrated primary care. Students learn the Pathways of Care model, developed at ASU, and a framework for clinical and business success in health care reform.

The DBH is an 84 credit hour program that is available via ASU Sync or in an immersive, in-person format. Students may use 30 credit hours from a master's degree toward the total 84 credit hours, leaving 54 credit hours required. The final project for the degree is a capstone applied research project that is completed in the student's final year. The program requires 240 internship hours.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of roles within integrated health care, including:
- behavioral health consultant in primary care
- behavioral health manager in a primary care system
- clinical director of behavioral health in a hospital or clinic system
- owner and operator of an integrated health care company
- trainer in behavioral health

The PhD program in biochemistry provides students with training at the cutting edge of biochemical research. Coursework and extensive research training prepare students for careers in academia, government and industry.

Students are required to carry out original and significant research in a specialized area of biochemistry. Specializations are available in all major areas of modern biochemistry and molecular biology, including:

    bioenergetics and photosynthesis
    biomolecular structure and function
    drug design and discovery
    enzymology and catalysis
    genetics and molecular biology
    neurochemistry
    protein folding and misfolding
    signal transduction

The curriculum offers an interdisciplinary education in modern biochemistry. Faculty from many departments, schools and centers participate in the program.

The MS program in biological data science provides students with the real-world skills needed to manage and analyze high-dimensional data sets in biomedical research.

The program focuses on developing a strong foundation in biology, statistics and computation. Students are trained in the latest data science technologies as they apply to biology and will be able to manage and analyze big data sets in genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and other modern life sciences areas. They learn to identify and implement appropriate solutions to manage and analyze data and to effectively collaborate on research projects with a team of investigators from different scientific backgrounds.

The program curriculum is designed and updated to meet the growing demands of academic and industrial research for trained data scientists. It provides rigorous training in data science for biological systems, using cutting-edge tools. Through real-world, hands-on learning experiences, students apply the skills acquired in the program. Students apply computational and statistical thinking to a wide range of biological problems. They practice verbal and written communication skills and develop project management strategies to complete a capstone project.

As a rapidly emerging field in the life sciences, data science and bioinformatics are constantly evolving; therefore, the program's curriculum is constantly updated with new material to reflect the rapid advances in the field.
Program name: Biological Data Science, Master of Science

description:
The Master of Science program in biomedical engineering provides students with in-depth knowledge in specialized areas of biomedical engineering. Students can customize their course of study with a variety of emphasis areas, and they will graduate prepared to lead research and development efforts in a variety of health care-related fields.

In this program, students have two options: the thesis option and the nonthesis option. The thesis option allows students to conduct independent research, mentored by an expert faculty member, and is excellent preparation for further graduate studies or for research and development careers in industry. The nonthesis option provides a course-based curriculum, which may include an independent research project and report, that is designed to prepare graduates for professional careers in the biotechnology and biomedical industries.

The PhD program in biomedical engineering prepares students for careers in academic and industrial research and development. The program trains students to recognize and identify important problems in medicine and biology and to apply engineering principles in developing innovative and effective solutions. The program emphasizes an interdisciplinary approach to research to effectively bridge the engineering and medical disciplines.

Graduates of the doctoral program are in high demand in both industry and academia. For those who choose to enter industry, the problem-solving and critical-thinking skills learned through doctoral training are vital for developing and managing new products and intellectual property. The academic skills learned in the PhD program (e.g., teaching, grant writing, mentoring and research) provide the foundation for a successful academic career.

The MS program in biomedical informatics provides students with the knowledge and skills to develop and apply cutting-edge computational methods to better understand, diagnose, treat and prevent human diseases.

The curriculum is built upon a multidisciplinary training in quantitative sciences such as statistics and computer science combined with basic biological and clinical sciences. Students gain in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in a variety of biomedical informatics areas, including:
- bioinformatics
- clinical informatics
- imaging informatics
- population health informatics
- sensor informatics

Graduates of this master's degree program are well prepared to advance to doctoral studies in biomedical informatics and related fields, or to pursue careers in the health care industry and in academic research environments.

The PhD program in biomedical informatics is a research-intensive program that prepares the next generation of leaders to make novel contributions to the field that advance the science of biomedical informatics and improve human health. The program provides students with the skills to conduct fundamental and translational research in a variety of biomedical informatics subdomains, including:
- bioinformatics
- clinical and translational research informatics
- consumer health informatics
- health informatics management
- imaging informatics
- population health informatics
Students engage in research early and throughout their training. They conduct independent research, write grant proposals, mentor junior students, submit and publish manuscripts, present at national meetings and defend their dissertation research. Coursework emphasizes fundamental knowledge that is essential for all biomedical informaticians, such as the organization of biomedical data, the effective use of biomedical information systems and the integration of machine learning and artificial intelligence to inform health care. All students are individually mentored and develop a flexible and individualized program of study that aligns with their professional goals.
The program is administered by the Department of Biomedical Informatics, which is located on the Phoenix Bioscience Core. The department is housed in the College of Health Solutions and has a collaborative relationship with Mayo Clinic. Students have a wide variety of research opportunities available with faculty from the Department of Biomedical Informatics, other ASU departments and colleges, and local health care and research partners, including Mayo Clinic, Banner Health, HonorHealth, Phoenix Children's Hospital and the Translational Genomics Research Institute.

Concentration name: ['Business Analytics', 'Consulting', 'Entrepreneurship and Innovation', 'Finance', 'Information Management', 'Leadership and Change', 'Marketing', 'Supply Chain Management']
description:
The W. P. Carey Master of Business Administration offers a world-class business education and highly ranked programs. Through a curriculum that is personalized to each student's goals, the W. P. Carey MBA prepares students for success in a variety of careers.

The Full-time MBA program helps students to recognize their unique purpose and passion and to build an MBA experience that supports that. By identifying an area of emphasis and through a customized selection of electives, students gain both the breadth and depth of skills and knowledge desired by top companies.

MBA students are part of a collaborative and supportive community, but they are also competitive and driven to achieve their goals. The W. P. Carey School provides a wide array of career resources, including a dedicated career services center, to help students identify the best career path and to provide the tools and support to get them there. The MBA curriculum includes a required internship for all two-year students, which delivers important, hands-on experience and often leads to full-time job offers. There are also opportunities to gain global experience through a variety of international study programs.

Graduates are prepared to advance in their careers and to take on leadership positions in a wide variety of industries and functions.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top-ranked business schools in the United States and is internationally recognized for its leadership in business education. The school is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The Master of Science in business analytics is a STEM-designated program offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business. It is designed for recent college graduates who are interested in pursuing a career in the rapidly growing field of business analytics.

The program provides students with the skills needed to succeed in data-rich business environments. Students learn how to analyze large data sets and apply the results to solve business problems, a skill set that is in high demand in today's job market.

Students learn from leading faculty in the field who are known for their research in data mining, business intelligence, data warehousing, statistical modeling, optimization and supply chain analytics. The curriculum focuses on business applications of analytics and provides hands-on experience with the leading data analytics tools and techniques. The program's content is continuously updated by an advisory board composed of senior analytics managers at top-tier firms.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The MS program in chemical engineering provides advanced instruction and research experience, preparing students to contribute to research and development in a broad range of industries, including energy, environment, materials, semiconductors, biotechnology and pharmaceuticals.

Students develop expertise in the core chemical engineering areas of transport phenomena, thermodynamics, kinetics and reaction engineering, and applied mathematics, along with independent research experience. They also have the opportunity for advanced study in a variety of specialized areas, such as biochemical and biomedical engineering, catalysis, energy systems, materials science, and environmental and sustainable engineering.

The program is flexible to accommodate students with a variety of career objectives. Students seeking a terminal master's degree can select one of the following options: a thesis option that offers a research-oriented experience or a nonthesis option with an applied project. Students who plan to continue on to a doctoral program will have an opportunity to participate in leading-edge research with faculty who are leaders in their fields.

The PhD program in chemical engineering provides students an opportunity to pursue research at the cutting edge of modern chemical engineering with a world-class faculty. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in chemical engineering principles and to develop the skills necessary to become independent researchers and leaders in their field.

The program is flexible and allows students to tailor their coursework and research to their individual interests. The curriculum includes core courses in transport phenomena, thermodynamics and reaction engineering, as well as a wide range of elective courses in specialized areas such as:

-advanced materials
-biotechnology
-energy and sustainability
-environmental engineering

In addition to coursework, students conduct original research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. The research component of the program culminates in a written dissertation and an oral defense.

The chemical engineering program has a collaborative and interdisciplinary culture. Close ties with other engineering programs, the Biodesign Institute, and various centers of research excellence, such as the Center for Negative Carbon Emissions and the Arizona Center for Algae Technology and Innovation, provide numerous opportunities for students to gain broad expertise and conduct interdisciplinary research.

The PhD program in chemistry provides students with the opportunity to pursue advanced study and research in a specific area of chemistry. The curriculum prepares students for careers in research or academia.

Students are immersed in a culture of research from the first day of the program. The curriculum combines an advanced, customized course of study along with dissertation research conducted under the guidance of a research advisor and supervisory committee.

During the first year of study, students take core graduate courses in a major area of chemistry and choose a research group. After the first year, students focus on their own research projects that will ultimately culminate in a dissertation. Students are expected to publish their original research in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals.

This is a research-intensive program in which students are financially supported through teaching or research assistantships, including a tuition waiver and health insurance. Several fellowships are also available for highly qualified students. Students are trained to think critically and creatively and to become independent scientists who can address today's major scientific challenges.

The PhD program in Chicana and Chicano studies provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the historical and contemporary experiences of Chicanos and Chicanas. The PhD is an interdisciplinary degree that reflects the intellectual and practical histories that inform the field of Chicana and Chicano studies. Program faculty are committed to scholarship that advances social justice.

The faculty prepares students with a deep understanding of qualitative research methods to conduct original research projects that reflect intellectual rigor and a commitment to address pressing social problems.

The School of Transborder Studies is a vibrant intellectual space with faculty whose work influences national and international discussions about a wide range of fields in the social sciences and humanities. The faculty's expertise is broad and includes history, sociology, anthropology, political science, women and gender studies, cultural studies, literature, performance studies, music and art. Students benefit from the interdisciplinary nature of the faculty's research and the school's intellectual life.

The online graduate certificate in child and family leadership is a 15-credit-hour program that offers professionals from a wide range of fields advanced training in child development and in leading programs and policies that support families with young children. Students learn from world-renowned faculty at the T. Denny Sanford School of Social and Family Dynamics. This program builds on students' diverse experiences in health care, social services, law, education, family support and other community-based professions. Students in this program receive a high-quality education as they build expertise and credentials that position them for career advancement. Coursework provides students with the foundational knowledge of child development from birth through age 8 and the knowledge and skills necessary to lead the development, implementation and evaluation of programs, policies and systems that support young children and their families.
Program name: Child and Family Leadership, Graduate Certificate

Concentration name: construction engineering, environmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, hydrosystems engineering, materials engineering, structural engineering, transportation engineering
description:
The PhD program in civil, environmental and sustainable engineering prepares students for careers in research and academia in one of the seven specialty areas of the School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment:

*   construction engineering
*   environmental engineering
*   geotechnical engineering
*   hydrosystems engineering
*   materials engineering
*   structural engineering
*   transportation engineering

The doctoral program requires 84 credit hours, which include 30 credit hours from a master's degree in a related field. The 54 credit hours required beyond the master's degree include 30 credit hours of coursework and 24 credit hours for dissertation and research.

The coursework consists of an approved program of graduate courses that includes six to 12 credit hours of mathematics and 18 to 24 credit hours in a major specialty area. In addition, students must pass a qualifying examination, a comprehensive examination and a dissertation defense. Students also are expected to participate in the graduate student seminar series.
Program name: Civil, Environmental and Sustainable Engineering, PhD

description:
The clinical exercise physiology master's degree program prepares students for careers in cardiac and pulmonary rehabilitation, as well as in other clinical and community settings in which exercise is used for the prevention and treatment of chronic disease. The program can also serve as a pathway to doctoral programs (e.g., PhD or MD).

Coursework and labs provide a strong foundation in the physiological and pathophysiological bases of exercise for both healthy people and people with chronic diseases. Hands-on clinical training is central to the curriculum, and students complete a 600-hour internship at a local hospital or other clinical facility.

The program is designed to meet the requirements for professional certification through the American College of Sports Medicine, which is generally a requirement for employment in the field. Students are eligible to take the Certified Clinical Exercise Physiologist® exam upon completion of the program. Students who are already certified may apply for a waiver for some or all of the internship hours.

The MS in clinical exercise physiology prepares graduates for a career with a focus on applying physical activity and behavior change strategies to assist individuals with or at risk of chronic disease and other medical conditions to improve their physical fitness, health and quality of life. For graduates who have already obtained certification, this advanced degree may see enhanced career opportunities.
Accreditation status: The Clinical Exercise Physiology, MS program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs upon the recommendation of the Committee on Accreditation for the Exercise Sciences.
Program name: Clinical Exercise Physiology, Master of Science

description: The Master of Arts program in communication, offered by the Hugh Downs School of Human Communication, is designed for students who are interested in pursuing advanced studies in human communication. The program provides opportunities for study in one or more of the school's core areas of specialization: health communication, interpersonal communication, intercultural communication, organizational communication, performance studies, and rhetoric and public communication. Students are introduced to multiple theoretical perspectives and research methodologies for the study of human communication, and they are challenged to develop and pursue an individualized program of study consistent with their own intellectual and professional goals. The curriculum is intended to provide students a broad-based background in communication theory and research.

The PhD program in communication at the Hugh Downs School of Human Communication is an advanced research degree that prepares students to be professional scholars.

The program focuses on training students to conduct original research that makes a significant contribution to scholarship in the discipline and to effectively teach at the college and university level.

Coursework provides a thorough grounding in the communication discipline, with an emphasis on the social sciences and humanities. A close working relationship between the student and a faculty advisor is at the core of the program. After completion of core courses, a student's program of study is composed in close consultation with an advisory committee, which assists in tailoring a series of courses, seminars and research experiences to fit the student's unique intellectual interests.

The PhD program in community resources and development prepares students to become transdisciplinary scholars and leaders in community development.

Graduates are able to facilitate sustainable and equitable change by examining the social, economic, environmental and political factors that shape communities. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, government, nonprofit organizations and private industry where they can advance community development theory, practice and policy.

The curriculum provides a strong theoretical and methodological foundation. Students are mentored throughout the program by nationally and internationally recognized faculty who share a commitment to engaged scholarship for public good. With a low student-to-faculty ratio, the program allows students to customize their program of study to meet their research interests and career goals. Students choose an area of specialization where they develop expertise in an area of community development. Example areas of specialization include:

*   community development, including parks, recreation and event management
*   nonprofits and nongovernmental organizations
*   public policy and community development
*   sustainable communities, including sustainable tourism
*   youth development

The curriculum is transdisciplinary by design. Students are encouraged to develop a program of study that crosses disciplines by taking coursework within the school and across the university.

The MS degree program in community resources and development with a concentration in parks and recreation management is one of the leading programs of its kind. The program provides the advanced expertise needed by professionals responsible for the planning, management and delivery of parks, recreation, tourism and related services.

Students learn from a renowned faculty who provide expertise in a wide variety of specializations and who are committed to providing students with high-quality educational experiences.

The curriculum is flexible to ensure students achieve their individual career objectives, and it offers opportunities for research and practical experience. Students may develop expertise in such areas as:

community sports management
public lands and recreation management
recreational therapy
tourism and special events
Program name: Community Resources and Development - Parks and Recreation Management, Master of Science

description:
The Master of Science program in computer engineering with a concentration in computer systems offers students a cutting-edge education, research and innovation in computer engineering.

Computer systems research at ASU involves an inclusive view of the computer system stack. Students build a strong foundation in computer architecture, software systems and network protocols. They may also pursue research in specific advanced areas, including:

- architecture for embedded, mobile, cloud and high-performance computing systems
- compilers
- computer networks
- distributed systems
- operating systems
- storage systems
- virtualization

Coursework and research in these areas leads to graduates who are sought after by a wide variety of employers in the U.S. and around the world.
Program name: Computer Engineering - Computer Systems, Master of Science

description: The Master of Science program in computer engineering with a concentration in electrical engineering offers both a thesis and a nonthesis option and provides a comprehensive, high-quality course of study in preparation for a career in industry or for advanced study in a doctoral program. The program gives students the flexibility to pursue a broad range of topics, from computer architecture to VLSI, and it culminates with an opportunity to conduct independent research under the supervision of a faculty member. The electrical engineering concentration emphasizes the physical design and implementation of computing systems. Students must complete a final examination in which they defend a thesis or, in the nonthesis option, present their portfolio.
Program name: Computer Engineering - Electrical Engineering, Master of Science

description: The Master of Science program in computer science provides students with an in-depth education in computer science and is for those who wish to either continue to the doctoral program or pursue a career in industry. Students must complete a course of study and a thesis or a nonthesis option. The nonthesis option requires additional coursework, including a capstone course. A portfolio is required for both thesis and nonthesis students upon graduation. The MS program offers a general computer science track as well as a concentration in big data systems and a concentration in cybersecurity. Students in the general track take courses that cover the breadth of computer science topics. The big data systems concentration provides students a strong foundation in the principles and practice of developing scalable systems and applications for data science. The cybersecurity concentration provides students an in-depth education in the security of computer systems and networks.

The PhD program in computer science is an advanced, research-based degree program in the School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence. The school has a worldwide reputation for its research programs, with particular strengths in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data management and analysis, embedded and distributed systems, and graphics and visual computing. Students in this doctoral program choose from and conduct in-depth research in one of a variety of areas of specialization. The program prepares students to become researchers in an industrial or academic setting.

The Master of Science program in construction management and technology is a graduate-level program that offers students advanced studies in construction management and technology. The program prepares graduates for leadership roles in the construction industry.

The program has two concentrations: facility management and general construction.

The general construction concentration allows students to select from an array of technical courses that meet their individual career goals. This concentration is a good choice for students with bachelor's degrees in construction, architecture or engineering.

The facility management concentration prepares students to plan, manage and operate the physical assets of a corporation or institution. Coursework includes construction operations, life cycle cost analysis and facility management technology. This concentration is a good choice for students with bachelor's degrees in construction, architecture, business or engineering who wish to pursue a career as a facility manager.

The program offers both a thesis and nonthesis option. The thesis option requires 24 credit hours of coursework and a six-credit hour thesis, with a minimum of 18 credit hours of coursework within the major. The nonthesis option requires 30 credit hours of coursework, with a minimum of 18 credit hours within the major.

The Del E. Webb School of Construction is housed in the School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment, one of the eight Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering. The construction programs have a long history of success at ASU. The program has strong ties with the construction industry, a history of excellent student placement and an active alumni group.
Accreditation status: The Construction Management, MS program is accredited by the American Council for Construction Education. The program earned a six-year term of accreditation in 2023.
Program name: Construction Management and Technology, Master of Science

description:
The Master of Counseling program provides a comprehensive foundation for individuals aspiring to become professional counselors. It prepares students for state licensure and national certification examinations, enabling them to work in a variety of mental health settings.

The curriculum is grounded in evidence-based practices and emphasizes the development of essential counseling skills, multicultural competence and ethical decision-making. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, supervised practicum and internship experiences, students gain hands-on experience in assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning and intervention.

The program focuses on a range of counseling theories and techniques, allowing students to develop a versatile and integrative approach to therapy. Graduates are equipped to address the diverse needs of clients across the lifespan, including those with mental and emotional disorders, substance abuse issues and career development concerns. The program's commitment to social justice and advocacy prepares students to be leaders and change agents in their communities, promoting mental wellness and equitable access to care for all populations.

Students seeking admission to the Master of Counseling program must have a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution, a minimum GPA and satisfactory GRE scores.
Accreditation status: The master's degree program in counseling is accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs.

description:
The MFA program in creative writing at ASU is one of the most esteemed in the country. The program offers tracks in fiction and poetry and encourages students to develop their craft and literary aesthetics through a course of study that includes workshops, literature courses and a wide variety of electives. Students have many opportunities to teach creative writing in the community.

Classes are small, and students work closely with a distinguished faculty. The program, one of the first to be established in the Southwest, offers students an apprenticeship to the literary arts.

The creative writing program hosts an active reading and talk series, the ASU Visiting Writers and Editors Series, that brings to campus eight to 10 nationally known writers a year to read their work and to talk with students. The program is also home to a distinguished literary journal, Hayden's Ferry Review, which is edited by the graduate students.
Program name: Creative Writing, Master of Fine Arts

description: The Master of Arts in criminology and criminal justice is a degree program that provides students with a professional education that includes a solid foundation in criminology and criminal justice theory, program evaluation and research methodology. This graduate-level education is appropriate for students seeking to advance their careers as practitioners and administrators in criminal justice and related agencies, as well as for students wishing to pursue a doctoral degree. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in the justice system, such as in federal, state and local law enforcement; in adult and juvenile corrections and probation; in court administration; and in private sector occupations such as private security, investigation and loss prevention.

The PhD program in criminology and criminal justice at Arizona State University is a research-intensive program designed to produce highly skilled researchers who are prepared for careers in academic and research settings. The program is one of the top-ranked doctoral programs in the country according to U.S. News & World Report.

Students are trained by a faculty of nationally and internationally recognized scholars engaged in cutting-edge research across the spectrum of criminology and criminal justice. Students are required to work closely with at least one faculty member on a research project starting in their first year. Students gain valuable experience working on faculty research projects by becoming involved in all aspects of the research process, including grant writing, research design and data collection, data analysis, and manuscript preparation and publication.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in criminological theory and both quantitative and qualitative research methods. Graduates of the program will have a thorough grounding in theory, research methods and statistics and a demonstrated capacity to conduct high-quality independent research. The program prepares students to become leading scholars and researchers in the field.

Concentration name: ['art education concentration', 'early childhood education concentration', 'educational technology concentration', 'elementary education concentration', 'English education concentration', 'language and literacy concentration', 'mathematics education concentration', 'physical education concentration', 'science education concentration', 'social studies education concentration', 'special education concentration', 'special education - applied behavior analysis concentration']
description:
The PhD program in curriculum and instruction prepares students to become outstanding educational researchers and leaders. Students pursue original research in a specific concentration within the broader field of curriculum and instruction.

Graduates of this doctoral program become university professors, curriculum developers, researchers and school district leaders in their selected areas of study. They are highly skilled in research methodologies and well-versed in the latest theoretical and pedagogical developments in their fields.

This is a research-intensive degree program that involves students in ongoing research throughout their coursework. Students must take at least 15 credit hours of research courses, including an introduction to research, qualitative and quantitative research methods, and more advanced research courses selected with a faculty advisor's approval.

Students choose from one of the following concentrations:

applied behavior analysis
art education
early childhood education
educational technology
elementary education
English education
language and literacy
mathematics education
physical education
science education
social studies education
special education

This program includes a required internship in which students apply research and professional knowledge in a university teaching, research or service setting under the supervision of a faculty member. The program requires 24 credit hours of dissertation research.

The Master of Science program in cybersecurity provides a solid foundation for a career in the dynamic and ever-growing field of cybersecurity. It is designed to prepare students for careers in the private and public sector in areas such as network security, digital forensics and cyber operations.

The curriculum has a strong technical emphasis and a focus on providing hands-on experience in our state-of-the-art cybersecurity lab, also known as the ASU cyber-range.

The program offers a thesis and a nonthesis option. The nonthesis option includes the choice of a project or a portfolio.

This program has an option for an accelerated master's degree. Students can find more information on the school website.

The Master of Arts in data science, analytics and engineering with a concentration in computational models and data offers an innovative, flexible and interdisciplinary curriculum for students interested in developing knowledge and expertise in computational modeling, mathematical and statistical analysis, data management, big data, machine learning, and high-performance and distributed computing.

Students develop knowledge and expertise in the design, development and application of computational and data-driven models. They learn how to use these models to reason about and gain insights from heterogeneous data in order to support science, engineering and business decision-making. Students learn how to build and maintain large-scale software infrastructure for managing, processing and visualizing data throughout its life cycle and they learn how to address social, ethical and legal issues related to data science.

The program is distinguished by its interdisciplinary curriculum and faculty expertise. The School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence has world-class faculty in data science, including machine learning, data mining, visual analytics, high-performance and distributed computing, cloud computing, and cybersecurity. The School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences has world-class faculty in statistics, applied mathematics and computational mathematics. The combination of these two top-ranked schools offers students an unparalleled opportunity for in-depth training in the foundations and applications of data science.

Students can design a course of study with an emphasis on a particular application domain by taking courses from other programs at ASU in areas such as:
biomedical informatics
business analytics
earth and space exploration
engineering
geographic information systems
health
social sciences
Program name: Data Science, Analytics and Engineering (Computational Models and Data), Master of Arts

Concentration name: Industrial Design, Interior Design, Visual Communication Design
description:
The Master of Design in design is a transdisciplinary, research-based program that provides a post-professional education for designers from various disciplines, such as industrial design, interior design, graphic design, and architecture, who wish to pursue a specialization in a specific design area.

The Master of Design program provides a solid base of core design courses, research methods and theory, a special topics design studio and a master's studio. The curriculum is flexible and allows students to choose from a variety of elective courses in The Design School and across ASU. Students may also elect to complete a dual degree with the Master of Science in design.

The MDes program has a long tradition of producing leaders in the field of design, and graduates are well-prepared for a wide variety of career options, including roles in design research and strategy, service design, product and system design, user experience design and many others. Faculty members are committed to an integrated and transdisciplinary approach to design, and the program's curriculum emphasizes collaboration among students and faculty from different design disciplines. Students are prepared to excel in a rapidly evolving design profession.

The MDes program prepares students with the research and design skills to be thought leaders in their specific area of study. Graduates have a better understanding of how the various design disciplines intersect and influence each other, a necessary skill set for the future of design. The transdisciplinary approach is a key component of the program, and students have the opportunity to work with faculty and students from other design disciplines to explore new ideas and approaches to design. This unique approach allows students to gain a deeper understanding of design and its role in society. The curriculum is structured to support students to develop design research skills, advanced design skills, and the capacity to undertake independent research in their area of interest. This program produces graduates who are leaders in the field and prepared to design for a complex world.

Concentration name: Creative Practice (Art and Design), Cultural Data and Humanities, Learning and Education, Media, Physical Computing and Robotics, Public Engagement
description:
The Master of Arts in digital culture is a research-focused degree in which students work with a faculty mentor to produce a portfolio of scholarly and creative work. The program is specifically for students who may be interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in the field of arts, media and engineering or other related fields or who are interested in advanced practice in their fields of interest.

The program supports a wide range of fields of interest related to the digital culture concentration areas, which include: creative practice (art and design), cultural data and humanities, learning and education, media, physical computing and robotics, and public engagement.

Students pursue a course of study through a research group to develop advanced skills in their areas of interest and through interdisciplinary electives. The program culminates in a final portfolio that serves as the basis for application to a doctoral program or for a transition to professional practice.

The Master of Arts program in early childhood education offers students an interdisciplinary program of study focused on children from birth to age 8.

The curriculum is based on a constructivist and critical constructivist theoretical framework. This framework reflects a view of children as competent beings and active participants in their own learning and in the learning of those around them. Students are taught to see children as participants in a larger community with complex social, cultural and historical influences. The curriculum emphasizes the role of teachers as researchers and the importance of engaging in a process of inquiry and reflection.

The program is designed to develop early childhood leaders with a strong foundation in child development and learning, early childhood curriculum and pedagogy, inquiry, and advocacy and leadership.

The program supports practicing professionals to develop and refine the knowledge and skills they need to be effective early childhood leaders, advocates and teacher educators in a variety of settings.

Students complete an action research project or an applied project in the final semester of their program.

The PhD program in economics prepares students for careers as economists in academia, business and government. Graduates are equipped with a solid foundation in economic theory and quantitative methods, enabling them to conduct high-quality research in their chosen fields of specialization.

The doctoral program curriculum provides a thorough grounding in microeconomic theory, macroeconomic theory and econometrics. Building on this core, students develop expertise in a variety of specialized fields. All students complete a research paper in their second or third year of study and a dissertation in the later years of the program.

The Department of Economics has an international reputation for its distinctive research focus on applied and policy-oriented topics that rely upon a strong foundation in economic theory, institutional analysis and quantitative methods. The department has a large and diverse faculty with a wide range of research and policy interests.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Master of Arts in education program is an interdisciplinary program designed for students interested in studying issues in education from a variety of perspectives. The program allows students to focus on an area of interest within the field of education and can serve as a stepping stone to a doctoral program.

Students who complete this program gain the ability to analyze and critique educational policy, research and practice.

The Master of Arts degree in education requires 30 credit hours of coursework. All students must complete the 12 credit hours of required core courses. Students then choose 18 credit hours of electives based on their specific area of interest and in consultation with their advisor. As their culminating experience, all students must pass a written comprehensive examination.

The PhD program in education policy provides students with the theoretical and methodological tools necessary to conduct cutting-edge research on important issues facing educators and policymakers today. Students in the program develop a strong foundation in education policy research and also delve deeply into specific content areas, such as accountability, school choice, teacher policy and school finance.

The program features a faculty of leading scholars from the fields of education, economics and political science who are known for their influential research on education policy. These faculty members are deeply committed to training the next generation of education policy scholars, and they work closely with students throughout the program on research projects. Graduates of the program are well prepared to assume research and policy positions in academia, government and the nonprofit sector.

The PhD in education policy is offered through the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College, and it is also affiliated with the college's National Education Policy Center.

The Doctor of Education in leadership and innovation is a program for practicing educator-leaders who wish to create positive change in their profession. Graduates are equipped with the knowledge, skills and dispositions to lead innovation and change that result in improved educational outcomes and opportunities for all learners, particularly those in underserved communities.

The program of study is composed of core courses focused on leadership and innovation, research and methods courses focused on disciplined inquiry, and a concentration that allows for a deeper dive in a specific topic. Students may select from these concentrations:

P-12 Change Leadership for certified educators who desire to become principals, superintendents or other school or district leaders
higher education change leadership for those who want to be leaders in two-year and four-year colleges and universities
systems, professional and reimagined change leadership for those who want to be leaders in nonprofit, nongovernmental, community-based and other educational organizations

The principalship concentration prepares individuals to be leaders in P-12 school settings, including as principals, assistant principals and other administrators. The curriculum integrates leadership, research, and evaluation coursework with clinical practice. It meets the requirements for principal certification in the state of Arizona.

The Master of Arts in educational policy and evaluation prepares students with the knowledge and skills to lead reform and renewal in educational settings. Graduates pursue careers as policy analysts, researchers and evaluators in a wide variety of settings, including school districts, charter management organizations, state departments of education, regional laboratories, legislative offices and nonprofit and for-profit organizations that seek to advance educational opportunity.

Students complete a common core of courses that cover educational policy, research methods and data analysis and select a concentration of courses focused on a key area of educational policy and practice. The program culminates in an applied project that is a summative experience in which students work closely with a faculty member to design and execute a policy analysis or program evaluation that is directly relevant to their career goals and professional interests.

Graduates are trained to analyze local, state and federal policies and to evaluate the quality and effectiveness of educational programs. Students are also prepared for further graduate study at the doctoral level.

Concentration name: ['Communication, Networking and Signal Processing', 'Computer Engineering', 'Control Systems', 'Electromagnetics, Antennas and Microwave Circuits', 'Electronic and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design', 'Physical Electronics, Photonics and Magnetics', 'Power Systems and Energy']
description:
The Master of Science in electrical engineering program provides students with the knowledge and skills needed for a successful career in electrical engineering. The graduate program emphasizes a student's chosen area of study through specialized coursework and research.

Students choose from seven concentration areas:

Communication, networking and signal processing --- this concentration focuses on the theory and application of information transmission and the processing of signals. Areas of research include communication and information theory, communication networks, data compression and coding, signal and image processing, statistical signal processing, video processing, and wireless communications and networks.

Computer engineering --- this concentration deals with the design, analysis and implementation of computer systems. Areas of specialization include computer architecture, computer-aided design and testing, embedded systems, and mobile and wireless computing.

Control systems --- this concentration studies the modeling, analysis and design of dynamic systems in order to modify their behavior. This concentration is a highly interdisciplinary subject with applications across all engineering disciplines. Areas of research include adaptive and learning control, automotive systems, control of manufacturing systems, nonlinear control, robust control, and sensor and data fusion.

Electromagnetics, antennas and microwave circuits --- this concentration focuses on the study of electromagnetic waves, their radiation, propagation, scattering and interaction with materials. Areas of research include active and passive remote sensing, antenna theory and design, computational electromagnetics, electromagnetic properties of materials, microwave and millimeter-wave circuit and device design, and wave propagation.

Electronic and mixed-signal circuit design --- this concentration addresses the analysis and design of electronic circuits and systems. Areas of research include analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits, data converters, digital and memory circuits, low-power and low-voltage circuits, radio frequency circuits and systems, and wireline communication circuits.

Physical electronics, photonics and magnetics --- this concentration focuses on the study of electronic and optoelectronic materials and devices. Areas of research include flexible electronics, laser and optical engineering, magnetic materials and devices, MEMS and nanostructures, nanoelectronics, organic electronics, photovoltaics, quantum electronics, semiconductor materials and devices, and solid-state electronics.

Power systems and energy --- this concentration focuses on electric power and energy systems. Areas of research include power electronics, power quality, renewable energy, and restructured power systems.

Concentration name: ['electric power and energy systems', 'electromagnetics, antennas and microwave circuits', 'physical electronics and photonics', 'signal processing and communications', 'solid-state electronics']
description:
The PhD program in electrical engineering is for students interested in performing research in a specialized area. The program culminates in a doctoral dissertation that represents a significant and original contribution to the field.
