description: The Master of Legal Studies degree at ASU Law is a 30-credit hour program for those who want to learn about the law and legal system but who do not want to become lawyers. The MLS degree provides students with an understanding of the U.S. legal system and teaches them the legal and critical-thinking skills needed to succeed in their careers. The program is offered on campus and online.
Accreditation status: The program is offered through the Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law, an American Bar Association (ABA)-approved law school.

description:
The Master of Arts program in linguistics and applied linguistics provides students with a solid foundation in the study of language and prepares them for a variety of language-related careers or for doctoral studies.

Students in the program study the core areas of linguistics (phonology, syntax and semantics) as well as the more applied areas of the field (sociolinguistics, second language acquisition, pragmatics and discourse analysis). Students also take courses in research methodology to prepare them for their own independent research.

Students must complete a portfolio as their culminating experience. The portfolio is a collection of three revised research papers written for graduate seminars taken as part of the student's coursework in the MA program. The papers are chosen in consultation with the student's portfolio committee chair and are meant to demonstrate the student's mastery of particular areas of linguistics and applied linguistics and their readiness to conduct independent research in those areas.

The PhD program in linguistics and applied linguistics offers students an interdisciplinary course of study that addresses issues of language structure, language use and the application of linguistic knowledge to real-world concerns.
Students in the program work with faculty members from a range of academic units who are experts in their fields and have diverse interests in linguistics and applied linguistics. Research foci include:
bilingualism and second language acquisition
corpus linguistics
discourse analysis
English linguistics
functional linguistics
historical linguistics
language policy and planning
linguistic anthropology
phonetics and phonology
pragmatics
sociolinguistics
syntax
TESOL
world Englishes
Graduates are well prepared to assume positions in academic, government or industrial settings. They have gone on to research and teaching careers at institutions in the U.S. and around the world, including the University of California at Berkeley, the University of Texas at Arlington, the University of Illinois at Chicago, the University of Michigan, Georgetown University, Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, the University of Alabama, the University of Hong Kong, King Saud University and Bilkent University. Other graduates work in the private sector for organizations such as Google, Microsoft and Intel, and for nonprofit and governmental agencies such as the U.S. State Department and the Center for Applied Linguistics.
Accreditation status: Higher Learning Commission

description:
The Master of Science in management is a business degree for students with an undergraduate degree in a field other than business. It offers a comprehensive set of foundational courses for those aspiring to a career in management.

The Master of Science in management curriculum is designed to provide students with the functional business skills to assume managerial roles in a wide range of industries.

The curriculum of 30 credit hours offers a comprehensive set of business courses designed to provide students with foundational skills in accounting, economics, finance, management, marketing and supply chain management.

Students who are unable to start in the fall may apply for a spring start. Please check with an advisor to discuss options.
Accreditation status: W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Master of Science in marketing is a specialized program that provides students with a theoretical foundation in marketing, as well as analytical and practical skills. The curriculum focuses on the strategic role of marketing in the firm, integrating product, pricing, promotion and place in a digital world.

The program is specifically designed to meet the growing need in firms for professionals who are analytically skilled and who can use in-depth knowledge of marketing to make business decisions. Students gain expertise in a variety of key marketing functions, including:
brand management
data analytics
digital marketing
market research

The curriculum provides a deep understanding of marketing functions and provides hands-on opportunities to apply knowledge in real business situations.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The doctoral program in mass communication, offered by the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication, prepares students for careers in academia and industry. The program emphasizes a strong foundation in communication theory and a variety of research methods.

The Cronkite School is a national leader in journalism and mass communication education, with a national reputation for its professional, hands-on programs. The school's doctoral program builds on that reputation, immersing students in a vibrant scholarly environment at a top-tier research university.

Located in a new, state-of-the-art facility in the heart of the nation's fifth-largest city, the school has many connections with local, national and international media organizations. Doctoral students have the opportunity to work with some of the top scholars and professionals in the field, including Pulitzer Prize-winning journalists and leading mass communication researchers. Doctoral students are matched with faculty mentors and work with them on research projects that are presented at academic conferences and published in peer-reviewed journals. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for faculty positions at research universities and for high-level research positions in the private sector.
Accreditation status: Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications

description:
The Master of Science program in materials science and engineering offers a thesis and a nonthesis option. The program provides advanced-level knowledge and training in the structure, properties, processing and performance of materials. This program helps prepare students for careers in industry or for further graduate study.

Students can choose to concentrate on a specific materials area, such as electronic, photonic and magnetic materials, materials for energy and sustainability, structural and mechanical properties, biomaterials, or materials computation and theory. However, the program is very flexible and students can design their coursework program to suit their particular needs. The program includes the study of ceramics, composites, metals, polymers and semiconductors.

The doctoral program in materials science and engineering is a comprehensive, research-based course of study covering the synthesis and processing, structure, properties and performance of materials. This interdisciplinary program in the School for Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy provides students with a strong background in materials science and engineering fundamentals, through a common core of courses. Students may then focus on one of many specialized areas of materials research.

The program emphasizes materials research, and students conduct in-depth research at a level that results in significant contributions to the field. This research, in the form of a dissertation, forms the major component of the degree requirements. The research is conducted under the guidance of a faculty member with expertise in the chosen area of study.

The MA in mathematics program is ideal preparation for a career in community college teaching, industrial mathematics or for entry into a doctoral program in the mathematical sciences.
Students in this program receive excellent classroom instruction, opportunities to participate in research and training alongside world-class faculty, and personal attention from their mentors. The program's diverse and active research faculty work in core areas of mathematics, applied mathematics, statistics and mathematics education.
The faculty members in the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences are dedicated to helping their students succeed. The school has a vibrant colloquium series and several weekly research seminars in various fields, with regular opportunities for students to meet and interact with visiting scholars. Other resources include an extensive university library system and a school-run computing facility. The school works with students to help them explore career paths and to prepare them for their future. Graduates with a mathematics master's degree are well prepared to go on to top-tier doctoral programs and to careers in business, industry and education.

Concentration name: ['Applied Mathematics', 'Computational Mathematics', 'Mathematics', 'Mathematics Education', 'Statistics', 'Analysis', 'Dynamical Systems', 'Geometry-Topology', 'Number Theory and Computational Mathematics']
description:
The PhD program in mathematics offers a broad training in mathematics and prepares students for careers in research and teaching at the university level as well as research in industrial or government laboratories.

All students are required to write and defend a dissertation. The final examination is an oral defense of the dissertation.

Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers. Many of our graduates hold academic positions in universities and colleges throughout the U.S. and around the world. Others work in government and in the industrial and financial sectors.

Students in the doctoral program have access to world-class faculty and state-of-the-art research facilities. They participate in research seminars, colloquia and annual conferences and workshops.

Research opportunities are available in several areas, including:

* analysis
* computational mathematics
* differential equations and dynamical systems
* geometry
* graph theory
* mathematical biology
* mathematics education
* number theory
* statistics

The MS program in mechanical engineering offers students an opportunity to advance their knowledge in the field and to engage in cutting-edge research with faculty in their chosen area of study. The School for Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy has a large and diverse faculty with a wide variety of research interests and expertise. Specific areas of study include:

control systems
design and manufacturing
dynamics and vibrations
solid mechanics and materials
thermofluids and energy

The program offers thesis and nonthesis options. Students in both options take a similar number of credit hours of coursework; however, nonthesis students take more coursework credit hours in lieu of thesis research, culminating in a comprehensive exam. The thesis option requires the completion of an original research project, a written thesis and an oral defense.

The PhD program in mechanical engineering is a research-oriented degree program. It provides students with an opportunity to work with world-class faculty on high-impact research topics and make a scholarly contribution to the mechanical engineering field.

The School of Engineering of Matter, Transport and Energy supports a highly interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment. Students work with faculty on research in a broad range of areas, including:

- autonomous vehicles and robotics
- computational mechanics and sciences
- controls and dynamical systems
- energy and transport systems
- manufacturing and materials
- solids, materials and structures

Students are trained to become independent researchers and scholars, gaining in-depth knowledge in their chosen field of study. Graduates of the program are well prepared for careers in academia, industrial research and development, and government agencies.

The PhD program in microbiology focuses on the study of microorganisms, including bacteria, archaea, viruses, yeasts, and protozoa, and their roles in medicine, industry and the environment. The program provides the intellectual foundation and technical training for students to carry out high-level research and contributes to the education and training of future generations of microbiologists.

Doctoral students conduct original research in their chosen field of study that culminates in a dissertation. Research opportunities are available in faculty laboratories in a wide range of fields, including applied and environmental microbiology, astrobiology, bacterial and archaeal diversity, bacterial pathogenesis, host-pathogen interactions, microbial cell biology, microbial ecology, microbial evolution, microbial genetics, microbial physiology, molecular virology and synthetic microbiology. The flexible curriculum and choice of rotation laboratories in the first year allow students to customize their course of study to meet their individual research interests.

Concentration name: ['Music (Collaborative Piano)', 'Music (Conducting)', 'Music (Interdisciplinary Digital Media and Performance)', 'Music (Music Composition)', 'Music (Music Performance)', 'Music (Music Research and Pedagogy)', 'Music (Musicology)', 'Music (Performance Pedagogy)', 'Music (Piano Pedagogy)']
description:
The Doctor of Musical Arts in music is an advanced, professional degree that prepares students for careers as artist-performers, artist-teachers and composers who are also qualified to teach in colleges and universities. The School of Music, Dance and Theatre offers DMA concentrations in collaborative piano, conducting, interdisciplinary digital media and performance, music composition, music performance, music research and pedagogy, musicology, performance pedagogy and piano pedagogy.

The doctoral program in music has as its goals: the development of the highest level of professional artistry in a major area of concentration, the expansion of knowledge and musical understanding in a cognate area of specialization, and the pursuit of advanced scholarship as it applies to music. The DMA degree represents the culmination of a student's formal education. Graduates are expected to possess the potential to make significant contributions to the music profession and to maintain an active involvement with a broad range of related academic and artistic disciplines. The DMA program offers students in-depth and specialized studies to pursue the highest levels of professional and academic achievements. The School of Music, Dance and Theatre's goal is to produce graduates who demonstrate outstanding artistry as professional musicians.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Dance and Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music.

Concentration name: ['Composition', 'Conducting', 'Music Education', 'Music Performance (Keyboard)', 'Music Performance (Strings, Voice, Winds, Brass, Percussion)', 'Music Theory', 'Music Therapy', 'Musicology', 'Performance Pedagogy', 'Popular Music']
description: The Master of Music degree program at ASU offers comprehensive and specialized graduate-level studies in music, emphasizing the development of students' abilities as performers, scholars and creative artists. Students admitted to the Master of Music program complete a major in one of 10 concentrations and a minor in music or in another field. The final project in the major area is a capstone experience and may take the form of a performance, a research paper or a lecture-recital.
Accreditation status: The music, music therapy, music theatre and dance programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music, the National Association of Schools of Dance, the National Association of Schools of Theatre, and the American Music Therapy Association, respectively. The teacher education programs are accredited by the Arizona State Board of Education.

description:
The Doctor of Philosophy program in music education provides students with a high level of scholarship in the theory and practice of music education, qualifying them for positions as university-level music education professors and as leaders of arts organizations and community music programs.

The curriculum is flexible to allow students to pursue individual interests, develop new insights and create innovative approaches to research. Coursework for the PhD in music education requires a strong core in music education, including coursework in research methods, psychology of music and sociology of music. A significant component of the program requires students to take coursework in a cognate area.

Doctoral students in music education have a strong record of publication and presentation at state, national and international conferences.

The Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts is home to a world-class faculty of scholars, artists and designers who are leaders in their fields. The music education faculty members have areas of expertise that include creativity, children's musical cultures, music teacher identity development and mentoring, social psychology of music, technology and the study of music in human life.
Accreditation status: Arizona State University is a member of and accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music.

description:
The PhD program in neuroscience at ASU provides world-class training in the study of the nervous system. The program's diverse faculty have expertise that ranges from the study of molecules and cells to systems and behavior.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in neuroscience, and students also receive in-depth training in statistics and experimental design.

The neuroscience PhD is an interdisciplinary program spanning multiple colleges and schools, providing students with a wealth of options for their research training and preparing them for a variety of careers in research and education.

Graduates are well-prepared for a variety of careers in research, education and industry.

Concentration name: ['Adult-Gerontology Nurse Practitioner', 'Advanced Nursing Practice', 'Family Nurse Practitioner', 'Family Psychiatric and Mental Health Nurse Practitioner', 'Innovation Leadership', 'Pediatric Nurse Practitioner', "Women's Health Nurse Practitioner"]
description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice degree program prepares graduates to perform at the highest level of advanced nursing practice. The program has two pathways for entry: the BSN to DNP pathway and the MS to DNP pathway, with multiple specialty options. The BSN to DNP pathway is for registered nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing who are seeking preparation in an advanced practice registered nursing or advanced systems specialty. The MS to DNP pathway is for registered nurses with a master's degree in nursing who are seeking preparation at the doctoral level. The program is designed for working professionals, is primarily online with minimal on-campus requirements, and is offered in a full-time or part-time format, depending on the specialty. On-campus requirements for the DNP program include orientation and final project defense. Students in advanced practice registered nursing specialties are also required to come to campus for an intensive session each semester. See the program website for a list of clinical specialties and their admission requirements. DNP graduates are prepared to be leaders in improving health outcomes for diverse populations and to translate research into practice. The program culminates in a final project that demonstrates the student's mastery of an area of advanced practice nursing.
Accreditation status: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master's degree program in nursing, Doctor of Nursing Practice program and post-graduate APRN certificate programs at Arizona State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org).

description:
The Doctor of Philosophy program in nursing at ASU's Edson College of Nursing and Health Innovation is a research-intensive, theory-based program designed to prepare expert nurse scientists who can conduct research and develop theories to advance nursing science and practice.

The PhD in nursing program provides a highly individualized course of study. The curriculum focuses on theory, research and practice to prepare nurse scientists to contribute to the body of knowledge in a substantive area of nursing. It provides students with a strong research foundation to launch a career in science. Graduates of this program are prepared for careers in a variety of settings where research, teaching and leadership are primary responsibilities, including academic institutions, research institutes and health care organizations.

Students choose their clinical populations and questions of interest from an array of areas, such as:
- health promotion
- health of individuals, families and communities
- disease prevention
- nursing education
- symptom science
- health care delivery and outcomes

Research core courses include advanced statistical analyses and the philosophical underpinnings of nursing science. Students select a substantive area of nursing in which they will focus their research and work closely with faculty who have expertise in that area. Students have the opportunity for individualized study with accomplished researchers whose interests match their own.

Upon completion of their coursework, students complete a comprehensive examination and a dissertation that makes an original contribution to nursing science.

The Master of Science program in nutrition in the College of Health Solutions provides advanced study of human nutrition. The program focuses on promoting health and well-being through food and nutrition. Students receive training to analyze and apply current nutrition research to projects and activities that focus on the health needs of individuals, groups and communities.

This degree program prepares nutrition professionals for leadership roles in a variety of settings. The program helps students apply and integrate knowledge of nutrient function with food and nutrition's role in health and disease. Students can advance their knowledge and skills in nutrition science, research, communication, counseling, technology and management. Faculty members are nationally and internationally recognized experts with a wide range of academic and research interests in nutrition.

The College of Health Solutions is dedicated to developing the health workforce of the future. The college is equipping students to influence smarter health choices, design better health care systems and promote the best health and well-being for individuals and communities.

This program culminates in a written thesis or an applied project. The applied project allows students to apply the skills and knowledge acquired in the program of study to a specific nutrition-related topic or question that is relevant to the student's area of interest or professional practice. This program produces graduates who go on to careers in research, academia, community, management, clinical and industry settings.
Accreditation status: The dietetics concentration of the MS in nutrition is an accredited program. | Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics

description:
The MA program in philosophy provides a solid foundation in the central areas of philosophy and is designed for students who want to pursue a doctorate in philosophy or who are interested in advanced study of philosophy for other professional or personal reasons.

Students in the philosophy master's program take seminars with doctoral students and receive the same rigorous training. They learn how to analyze and critically evaluate arguments, how to make and defend their own arguments, and how to present their work in both oral and written forms. Students also have the opportunity to take courses from affiliated faculty in other programs, such as law, biology and life sciences, and sustainability.

The program offers a traditional Master of Arts in philosophy and also an accelerated 4+1 Bachelor of Arts and Master of Arts for current ASU students.

Graduates are well-prepared to go on to top doctoral programs in philosophy or to pursue careers in law, public service and other fields that value clear and rigorous thinking.

The doctoral program in physics provides students with a superior education and training to conduct independent research in physics. It is designed to prepare students for careers in academic institutions, national laboratories and industrial research organizations. The research interests of the physics faculty are primarily focused in the areas of biophysics and soft matter, condensed matter and materials physics, cosmology and particle astrophysics, nuclear and particle physics, and physics education research.

The MA program in political science provides students with a strong foundation in the substance and methodology of political science. It is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in the public or private sectors, or who plan to pursue a doctoral degree.

The curriculum requires 30 credit hours and is divided into three components: a core of three required courses (9 credit hours), a major field of study (12 credit hours) and a supporting field of study or other electives (9 credit hours).

Students have the option to complete either a thesis or a nonthesis program. The thesis option is designed to be completed in two years of full-time study and requires an oral defense of the thesis. The nonthesis option requires a written comprehensive examination in the student's major field of study. The MA degree may be pursued on a part-time basis.

The doctoral program in political science provides students with the substantive and methodological knowledge needed to conduct research in political science. The program emphasizes a problem-oriented approach that applies rigorous theoretical and empirical methods to the study of politics and policy.

Concentration name: ['Behavioral Neuroscience', 'Clinical Psychology', 'Cognitive Science', 'Developmental Psychology', 'Quantitative Psychology', 'Social Psychology']
description: The doctoral program in psychology provides students with the best available training for careers in scientific psychology. The program is designed to develop in each student a sense of critical scholarship and an appreciation of the relationship between basic and applied research. The program emphasizes research, and all students are expected to become competent, productive researchers in their chosen areas of specialization. The degree prepares graduates for careers in research and teaching. Graduates are qualified to teach at the university level and to conduct research in academic or applied settings.
Accreditation status: The clinical psychology PhD program is accredited by the American Psychological Association.

Concentration name: Emergency Management, Local Government, Nonprofit Administration, Public Finance, Public Policy, Urban Management
description: The ASU Master of Public Administration program is a professional degree that provides students with the skills and knowledge to be a manager or leader in a public or nonprofit organization. This program gives students the tools to create innovative solutions to some of the most pressing challenges in public service. The MPA program's nationally recognized faculty are renowned for their expertise in public and nonprofit management, and they will challenge students to become more effective public service leaders. Students learn to address questions of accountability, effectiveness and equity in local, state, national and international government. Students also master skills in communication, analysis and problem-solving. This program is ranked No. 13 in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. The rankings are based on peer assessment surveys sent to deans, directors and department chairs at 285 schools of public affairs and administration.
Accreditation status: The Master of Public Administration program is accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration.

description:
The Master of Public Policy program equips students with the essential skills to understand and address complex societal problems that demand thoughtful and evidence-based solutions. The curriculum focuses on building a strong foundation in policy analysis, economics and data analysis, preparing students to be effective and ethical leaders in public service, nonprofit organizations and the private sector.

The MPP program stands out for its strong emphasis on the role of collaborative governance and public participation in the policy process, which provides students with a unique perspective on policy design and implementation. This approach to policy education prepares graduates to tackle the most pressing challenges of our time, from social and economic inequality to environmental sustainability.

Concentration name: Science and technology policy, Program evaluation and data analytics
description:
The PhD program in public policy at Arizona State University's School of Public Affairs is a research-based program designed to train scholars and practitioners to do policy-relevant research and analysis and to provide them with the knowledge and skills needed to enter academic and applied research careers in the public, private and nonprofit sectors.

The PhD in public policy is intentionally interdisciplinary. Students learn from faculty members from a wide range of disciplines, all of whom are committed to theoretically informed, empirically-grounded research. The program emphasizes a foundation in public policy theory and process, research design, and advanced quantitative and qualitative methods. In addition to a core curriculum, students select one of two emphasis areas: science and technology policy or program evaluation and data analytics.

The program is committed to producing graduates who can help meet the challenges and opportunities of a complex and increasingly diverse world.

The MA program in religious studies offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of religion. The curriculum focuses on the cultural, historical, political, social and philosophical aspects of religion as a category of human thought and experience. Students explore the diverse ways humans have constructed systems of meaning and value in global contexts, including traditions such as Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam and Judaism. Coursework also examines themes related to religion, including violence and peace, gender and sexuality, ritual and performance, and art and literature. The faculty specializes in the academic study of religion in a wide variety of ways, drawing upon the theories and methods of history, sociology, anthropology, ethics, philosophy and cultural studies. Students gain an advanced understanding of the major theories and methods in the study of religion and become familiar with the diverse religious traditions of the world.

Concentration name: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, Biomedical Systems, Robotics, Systems Engineering
description: The Master of Science program in robotics and autonomous systems provides a comprehensive, multidisciplinary, research-based education. Students gain a deep understanding of the principles of robotics and intelligent systems through coursework across multiple engineering and computer science disciplines. The program provides students the background needed to solve complex, interdisciplinary problems. Students in this program are prepared for careers that demand advanced knowledge in robotics, artificial intelligence and autonomous systems. Graduates are able to design, produce, and control the next generation of robotics and autonomous systems to address society's most pressing needs in areas that include health, transportation, supply chains and logistics, manufacturing, exploration, security and environmental stewardship. The curriculum is flexible and can be customized to the student's background and interests. Students can specialize in one of five concentration areas by taking at least three courses from an approved list for that concentration, or they can pursue a general robotics and autonomous systems degree.

The Master of Education in secondary education program is for students who have an undergraduate degree in a content area and want to become a certified teacher for grades 6-12. The program is specifically for those who do not yet have a teaching certificate.

The program allows students to complete their master's degree and teacher certification at the same time. The program focuses on research-based teaching strategies for working with students in today's diverse secondary classrooms.

As part of the program, students take part in a full-time residency, working with a highly qualified mentor teacher in a middle or high school. The residency provides an opportunity to develop teaching skills with the support and guidance of an experienced professional.

Students in the MEd in secondary education program select one of the following content areas for certification: biology, business, chemistry, earth and space science, economics, English, geography, history, mathematics, physics, political science or general science.

The program may be completed in 15 months, and coursework is offered in a combination of in-person, hybrid and online formats to support students' progress toward their degree.

Graduates are recommended for institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for teacher certification in their chosen content area for grades 6-12.

The Master of Arts program in social and cultural pedagogy focuses on the study of transformative learning and critical educational practices in a variety of social contexts, particularly in communities and workplaces. Social and cultural pedagogy is an internationally recognized field of research and practice with a long tradition of supporting human development and social justice through educational endeavors. It is an approach to education that is committed to promoting social inclusion, participation, and active citizenship by strengthening the capacity of individuals and communities to reflect upon their life circumstances and take action to improve their lives.

Students in the program examine the historical and philosophical foundations of pedagogy in relation to a range of social, cultural, political, economic, and ethical contexts. They also study contemporary educational theories and approaches to pedagogy and social transformation. The interdisciplinary curriculum connects with a wide range of academic disciplines, including justice studies, women and gender studies, ethnic studies, disability studies, and education. Graduates are prepared to use their knowledge and skills in various positions in nonprofit, community, and educational organizations.

The Master of Social Work program in the School of Social Work at Arizona State University prepares graduates for advanced social work practice with a curriculum that is continuously reviewed and revised to remain at the cutting-edge of social work education and practice.

The MSW degree program is fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education.

The curriculum is delivered in a variety of platforms to provide access for all individuals who desire to become a master's level social worker. These platforms include on-campus, online and a hybrid of on-campus and online.

Social workers with an MSW degree may obtain a license to practice clinical social work in all 50 states, and this program helps prepare graduates for social work licensure exams.

The MSW program has two concentrations: advanced generalist and advanced direct practice. All students, whether in the on-campus or online format, select one of these concentrations. The advanced direct practice concentration allows students to specialize in one of three areas: children, youth and families; health and behavioral health with adults; or public child welfare. The advanced generalist concentration is designed to prepare graduates to work effectively across all systems levels (micro, mezzo and macro) and fields of practice. The advanced generalist concentration is available through the Tucson campus only. The advanced direct practice concentration is available at the Downtown Phoenix, West and online campuses. Students in the on-campus program format may also pursue a certificate and concurrent degrees.
Accreditation status: The MSW degree program is fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education.

description:
The PhD in sociology provides students with the theoretical background and methodological skills to conduct sociological research, be effective teachers and become leaders in the field.

Students train for academic careers in sociology at research universities and liberal arts colleges as well as for careers in applied sociological research for the government or in the private sector. The doctoral program provides solid professional training that develops expertise in sociological theory and methods.

The Sanford School of Social and Family Dynamics offers an array of graduate courses that allows students to develop an individualized course of study emphasizing particular substantive fields, theories and methods. Students are also encouraged to take graduate courses in other academic units.

The faculty are committed to excellence in research and teaching and are nationally and internationally recognized for their expertise. Core areas of faculty expertise include:

*   education
*   family
*   health
*   migration
*   race and ethnicity
*   social networks
*   urban sociology

Faculty members have particular strengths in advanced statistical methods, comparative research and qualitative methods.

The Master of Science in software engineering program is designed for students with an undergraduate degree in computer science, software engineering, computer systems engineering or a very closely related field. It provides a foundation in the fundamentals of software engineering, with opportunities for students to specialize in areas of their interest. The curriculum focuses on preparing students for an industrial career or for advanced studies in a doctoral program.

The program helps students develop a strong foundation in software engineering principles, with emphasis on an engineering approach to the development of complex software-intensive systems.

Students learn how to:
apply lifecycle models, including requirements engineering, design, implementation and verification and validation
apply project management principles and practices
apply software quality assurance principles and practices
evaluate and select appropriate technologies for a given project
function as effective members of a software development team

The curriculum is structured to provide an in-depth study of specific software engineering topics and a comprehensive educational experience. This is accomplished through a selection of core courses and elective courses that cover all aspects of the software engineering process. Students have the opportunity to take specialized courses in areas such as:
cloud-native and microservice applications
distributed and dependable systems
DevOps and DevSecOps
embedded software systems
enterprise software systems
formal methods
mobile and web applications
model-based development
search-based software engineering
security engineering
software architecture and design patterns
software project, process and quality management
software testing and analysis

The program culminates in an applied project or a thesis. In the applied project, students use the knowledge and skills they have gained in the program to solve a real-world problem. In the thesis, students conduct research on a specific topic in software engineering and write a scholarly paper that presents their findings.

Concentration name: Early Childhood Special Education, Mild to Moderate Disabilities
description:
The MA in special education from Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College provides teachers and other professionals with advanced knowledge and skills for serving children, youth and adults with exceptionalities. This program offers two concentrations that lead to teacher certification in either mild to moderate disabilities or early childhood special education.

This master's degree program is offered entirely online and features the same high-quality instruction and curricula as the immersion program. Graduates become leaders in the field of special education, advocates for individuals with exceptionalities and their families, and collaborators with other professionals.

The special education MA is offered as an ASU Sync program. Students learn from faculty members who are nationally and internationally recognized for their contributions to research and practice in the field of special education. Students learn in a collaborative environment with their peers and program faculty and are prepared to work with a diverse student population in various school settings.

The MS program in speech and hearing science is a nonclinical degree that provides students with a broad base of knowledge in the processes of human communication and its disorders. Students gain a deep understanding of the fundamental processes of speech, language and hearing.

The program provides students with the advanced knowledge and skills necessary to pursue doctoral study in speech and hearing science, audiology or speech-language pathology or to work in a variety of settings.

Students learn from faculty members who are leaders in the fields of audiology and speech-language pathology and who are making a difference in the lives of individuals with communication challenges. They are active in research and provide excellent mentorship to students in the program.
Accreditation status: The master's degree program (MS) in speech-language pathology at Arizona State University is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard, #310, Rockville, MD 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.

description:
The Master of Sports Law and Business program is the only master's degree program in the nation that combines sports law and business in a single curriculum and is part of a law school. The Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law's Sports Law and Business program brings together the legal and business worlds to provide students with a unique and effective education. The curriculum includes sports-specific law and business courses and unparalleled externship opportunities. Taught by faculty with extensive experience in the sports industry, the program gives students the tools to take on leadership roles.

The Master of Sports Law and Business degree provides a deep understanding of the interplay between sports, law and business. Students learn a broad base of sports-related law and business concepts that they apply to real-life situations through project-based learning and an externship.

Students can also choose to focus on a particular area within the sports industry, such as:

NCAA rules and compliance
negotiation and alternative dispute resolution
professional and amateur sports law
sports media and business operations

These areas and others are addressed through both the curriculum and externships.

Through the program's extensive and expanding list of relationships with national and international sports organizations, students have opportunities to interact with top professionals. Graduates are prepared to succeed in the multifaceted sports industry.

The MS program in statistics provides students with a broad-based foundation in applied and theoretical statistics. Graduates of the program are well prepared for careers as professional statisticians in business, government and industry or to pursue doctoral degrees in statistics or a related field.

The statistics master's degree program is flexible and may be tailored to emphasize specific areas of application, such as:
biostatistics
computational statistics
environmental statistics
quality and reliability
statistics for business and economics
theoretical statistics

The statistics faculty in the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences are experts in a wide variety of areas, including:
Bayesian statistics
biostatistics and bioinformatics
computational statistics
design of experiments
environmental and ecological statistics
high-dimensional data analysis
longitudinal data analysis
modern regression
quality control and reliability
statistical genetics
theory of statistics
time series analysis

The Master of Arts in sustainability is a research-focused, thesis-based program. The curriculum provides students with a strong background in the theories and concepts of sustainability and equips them with the qualitative and quantitative analytical skills needed for careers that create and maintain sustainable systems.

The program provides an opportunity for students to pursue a specific area of interest within sustainability. Areas of study within the school include:

    cities and communities
    consumption and behavior
    decision-making under uncertainty
    energy, materials and technology
    equity and environmental justice
    food systems
    future studies
    governance and policy
    international development
    social transformations
    water

The transdisciplinary School of Sustainability is a hub for sustainability education and research at ASU. Its mission is to develop and share knowledge and to create and implement solutions to the most pressing sustainability challenges. The curriculum, developed by a world-class faculty of scholars and practitioners, trains the next generation of leaders and professionals to bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and practical application. Students learn to think in a systems-based, holistic way and to address the social, economic and environmental aspects of any challenge. The program prepares graduates who can create and implement sustainability solutions in a wide range of contexts.

Concentration name: ['Ecosystems sustainability', 'Policy and governance in sustainable systems', 'Sustainable energy, materials and technology', 'Sustainable food systems', 'Urban sustainability']
description:
The Master of Science in sustainability is a research-oriented degree program in the School of Sustainability. The program provides students with a substantive, transdisciplinary education in sustainability and problem-solving, with a focus on conducting research. The MS program culminates in a thesis or a capstone in the form of a publishable paper.

The curriculum includes a core of three required courses along with a set of methods courses and electives to complement the thesis or capstone project. Students learn from a renowned community of sustainability scholars and scientists and gain invaluable experience from the research they conduct. Each student also works with a faculty mentor for guidance.

Students in the Master of Science program select one of five tracks:
Ecosystems sustainability
Policy and governance in sustainable systems
Sustainable energy, materials and technology
Sustainable food systems
Urban sustainability

The MS in sustainability program is ideal for students who are interested in a research-based career and for graduates who go on to pursue a doctoral degree.

Concentration name: Urban sustainability, Ecosystem sustainability, Policy and governance in sustainable systems, Social transformations in sustainability, Sustainable energy, materials and technology
description:
The PhD program in sustainability prepares the next generation of scholar-activists to understand, research and develop solutions for the complex environmental, economic, social and cultural challenges of the 21st century. The curriculum provides a broad understanding of the concepts and methods of sustainability and an in-depth understanding of one or more related fields. The program promotes interdisciplinary connections with other ASU schools and departments. Graduates of this program are well prepared for a wide variety of careers in academia, government and industry.

The degree program offers five unique tracks:

Urban sustainability
Ecosystem sustainability
Policy and governance in sustainable systems
Social transformations in sustainability
Sustainable energy, materials and technology

Each of these tracks provides a lens through which students can view the world's pressing sustainability problems and potential solutions, as well as a focus from which to structure their own coursework, research and dissertation.

The program encourages students to move beyond the traditional academic disciplines to gain a deeper understanding of the complex interactions of human and natural systems. Sustainability scholars are problem-solvers who can cross traditional academic boundaries, integrate different kinds of knowledge, and link scholarship to real-world engagement.

The MS program in sustainable engineering is a transdisciplinary graduate degree program dedicated to addressing complex environmental, societal and economic problems. Students learn the tools of sustainability science and engineering with the goal of ensuring future human well-being and protecting the quality of life, the natural resource base and the ecological systems of the planet.

Students are educated on critical concepts and methods, such as:
- circular economy
- earth systems engineering and management
- industrial ecology
- life cycle assessment
- pollution prevention and control
- sustainable development
- systems thinking

The program provides a broad education through its core courses, while also allowing students to specialize through technical electives. Students can complete a thesis or a nonthesis option. The nonthesis option requires an applied project.

The systems engineering PhD program is for students who want to develop a fundamental understanding of systems theories and methodologies in order to address complex, real-world engineering and socio-technical problems.

The doctoral program in systems engineering provides the skills and knowledge necessary to perform advanced research in specialized areas of systems engineering and to successfully pursue research and development careers in academia, industry and government. The curriculum allows students to gain a strong foundation in the concepts of systems engineering and also provides flexibility for students to pursue their own research interests. Under the guidance of a faculty advisor, students choose electives in a specialized area that prepares them for dissertation research. The core coursework consists of a common set of subjects related to the fundamentals of systems engineering, and the program culminates with a dissertation that demonstrates a significant and original contribution to the field.

The MEd program in teaching is a graduate-level program that leads to a recommendation for an initial Arizona teaching certificate in secondary or elementary education.

This master's degree program is designed for students with a bachelor's degree in a field other than education who want to pursue a career in teaching. The program offers secondary education certification in the content areas of English, history, mathematics, political science or science (biology, chemistry, earth and space science, general science or physics). The program also offers elementary education certification for grades K–8.

Students work in collaborative cohorts with a group of approximately 25 students. Faculty members work with these small groups to provide an intensive, high-quality learning experience. The programs for both elementary and secondary education certification consist of a combination of coursework and a full-time, yearlong residency in a K–12 school. Upon completion of the program, students earn their master's degree and a recommendation for an Arizona teaching certificate.

The secondary education certification program places an emphasis on preparing teachers to work with the diverse student populations typically found in middle school and high school settings in Arizona. The elementary education certification program places an emphasis on preparing teachers to work with the diverse student populations typically found in K–8 school settings in Arizona.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the American Psychological Association and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages program provides students with a strong foundation in the theory and practice of second language teaching, learning and assessment. The degree prepares graduates for a wide range of English language teaching positions in the U.S. and abroad, including teaching in:

community language programs
immigrant and refugee resettlement organizations
private language schools
K-12 school systems (with appropriate state certification)
community colleges
universities
a variety of institutions abroad

Students learn from and collaborate with world-class faculty in the Department of English and have the opportunity to participate in cutting-edge research in linguistics and applied linguistics. Students are also supported in pursuing professional development opportunities like presenting at academic conferences and getting involved in professional organizations.

This program is offered by the Department of English, an academic unit of The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, and is one of the largest and most productive English departments in the U.S. The department is home to more than 300 award-winning faculty members who are national and international leaders in their fields.

ASU is a broadly diverse, service-oriented and community-engaged university. U.S. News & World Report has ranked ASU No. 1 among the Most Innovative Schools in America for the ninth consecutive year, and it is the highest-ranked university in the U.S. for innovation.
Program name: Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, MTESOL

description:
The MFA in theatre is a terminal degree and provides students the opportunity to specialize in one of three areas of study: acting, directing, or theatre for youth and community. Students work in a conservatory environment within a large research university.

The program emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical application, providing a variety of opportunities to apply students' learning and skills in production, including mainstage shows, student-directed projects, new work development, and work in the community.

The acting program is a three-year, 60-credit-hour program with a focus on stage, film and television acting and preparation for a career in the professional world.

The directing program has an international reputation for its focus on new work and new ways of working and for its focus on director-designer collaboration. Graduates of the program are working on Broadway, in major regional theatres, in film and television, and at universities around the world.

The theatre for youth and community program is one of the most respected in the U.S. and attracts students from around the world. It provides artists, scholars and educators with a flexible and individualized course of study for creating theatre and community-engaged arts programs with, by and for young people and communities.

The program is flexible and individualized, with students selecting courses and research topics that reflect their interests and career goals. Every student's program of study is unique. Students receive financial support and extensive teaching opportunities and are mentored by a faculty of practicing artists and scholars who are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields.
Accreditation status: National Association of Schools of Theatre, Accredited

description: The Master of Urban and Environmental Planning program in the School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning provides students with the background and skills to become professional planners, addressing complex social and environmental issues and planning for more sustainable, equitable, healthy, livable and economically vibrant communities. This is an accredited professional degree that prepares graduates for employment in the public, private and nonprofit sectors. The MUEP program addresses both urban and environmental planning and recognizes the inherent relationship between the two. The curriculum covers a broad range of planning subjects while encouraging depth in a specialization area.
Accreditation status: The Master of Urban and Environmental Planning is an accredited program of the Planning Accreditation Board (PAB), the official accrediting agency for master's degree programs in planning in the United States and Canada.

description:
The Doctor of Philosophy program in urban planning is a research-oriented degree. It is designed for students seeking careers in university teaching and research or in policy and research positions in the public, private or nonprofit sectors. The goal of the program is to educate a new generation of scholars and leaders with the substantive knowledge and research skills to address the critical challenges facing urban and metropolitan regions around the world.

The program emphasizes the development of theories, methodologies and their application in urban planning. It provides a strong substantive and methodological foundation, allowing students the flexibility to pursue their own specialized research interests.

Students tailor their programs of study in consultation with their advisors to focus on one of the following areas of interest:

Community development and housing: This area of study is focused on the social, economic and political dynamics of neighborhoods and communities, and their connections with the larger metropolitan area. Students focus on a range of topics including housing policy and finance, community-based planning, social justice, and international development.

Environmental planning: This area of study is focused on the theory and practice of integrating environmental concerns into urban and regional planning. Students focus on a range of topics, including sustainable development, environmental policy and social-ecological systems, water resource management, and climate change planning.

Land use and urban design: This area of study is focused on the built environment and the forces that shape it. Students focus on a range of topics, including land use planning and regulations, urban form and transportation, infill and redevelopment, and planning for healthy communities.

Transportation planning: This area of study is focused on the planning of transportation systems. Students focus on a range of topics, including transportation and land use, transportation policy and finance, transit planning and traffic modeling.

The doctoral curriculum provides students with rigorous training in planning theory, research design and methodology. The program structure offers both breadth in the various subfields of urban planning and depth within a student's particular area of interest, culminating in dissertation research that advances the knowledge of planning. Students will be prepared for successful careers in academia or in high-level policy and research positions where they can effectively address the challenges of planning in today's increasingly complex and globalized world.

The Master of Science in Design with a concentration in visual communication design is a two-year program for students with a background in design who want to elevate their careers and expertise as design leaders and educators.

This program attracts graduate students with a broad range of interests within the visual communication design field, including publication design, exhibition design, human-centered design, information design, interaction design, new media, social design, design research, design strategy and user experience design.

The Master of Science in Design with a concentration in visual communication design is a STEM-designated program. The curriculum focuses on expanding students' expertise and research in a specific area of interest. Coursework emphasizes design research methods and a thesis or applied project that demonstrates a graduate level of inquiry and expertise in a specific area of visual communication design.

As a research university, ASU focuses on expanding design knowledge. Graduate students' individual research pursuits are central to their studies, as is understanding research theory and methods.

The program fosters a small, cohesive student cohort, with faculty who are dedicated to graduate education and work closely with students as mentors. The faculty's diverse interests help students hone their own research interests. Each student is challenged to develop a unique area of specialization to research through their design work and writing.
Program name: Visual Communication Design, Master of Science in Design
